name_en: Jingmai Old Tree Purple Bud Shu
name_romanized: jǐng mài zǐ yá shú pǔ
aliases: Jingmai Old Tree Purple Bud Shou

brewing.notes: A safe starting point for ripe pu-erh: rinse once or twice, boiling water.

description:
Ripe pu-erh described as made from purple buds of old trees at Jingmai in Yunnan, seen as a 250 g tuo.

This is a tea plant cultivar rather than a finished tea, so you are more likely to meet its name in a grower's notes than on a packet. If you find tea made from it, brew it like any other ripe pu-erh tea and taste what the plant brings.
history: A 2007 pressing is on record. Little else is documented about it.
processing: A plant cultivar, not a processing style: it is usually made into ripe pu-erh tea, and the method is up to the grower.
harvest_season: Depends on the place and the grower.
appearance_dry: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_liquor: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_wet: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
taste_profile: Depends on how the leaf is processed; tea from it usually falls within what ripe pu-erh teas give.
